changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For ecommerce leaders with high-value orders: Orders dying at the last step cost you sales on your biggest baskets. Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance recover those orders, and we'll show you what each recovered order is worth to your business.
changes.why: Martin's 'same thing' objection came after the average-uplift slide failed to describe the loss in his terms, so the customer's own language about lost big-basket orders should replace the generic average.

changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For ecommerce teams losing sales at checkout: Recover the orders where the card says no, starting with your big baskets. Smart retries run automatically on each failed payment.
changes.why: The customer described the problem as orders dying at the last step on high-value baskets, so the recovery line should name that loss directly rather than describe the feature alone.

changes.change: For champions presenting to a CFO: A decline-cost business case built from your own payment export, showing lost order value next to gateway fees and chargebacks, which we can produce within days of receiving the export.
changes.why: Farah offered the decline analysis that would have answered the CFO's objection, Lucy asked for something to hand Martin, and the record shows nothing from us on failure cost reached him, so a fast standard leave-behind fills that gap.

changes.change: For buyers comparing processors: Compare total cost, including the value of declined orders, before discussing our rate. A rate counter alone does not change the value of the orders you are losing.
changes.why: The incumbent's only move was a rate cut that then replaced every other topic in the emails, so a total-cost framing gives the prospect a second number to weigh against any rate offer.
